_comment: Vignettes (Expansion 6 C.9, docs/ADVENTURES.md §6.11): hand-made situations, each needing particular things in the world (its vignette.needs, game/story/vignettes.py NEEDS), with its own meetings (v_...) and scenes (scenes.vignettes.json). Roles bound 'given' take what the need found; the need's words are the situation's own ({ruin}, {water}...).

note: The bell of {ruin_was} lies in the flooded crypt under {ruin}, where {water} came in the night {ruin_fall}.
Whatever lies in the drowned crypt under {ruin} has had {ruin_years} alone with the bell.

label: Tell me about the night it fell.
Why was the bell taken down at all?
say: They rang it to call the men in from the fields, the night {ruin_fall}. They rang it too long. It brought them straight to us. After, the ones who lived threw it in the water so it could never call anyone again.
It rang the whole night, child. Rang and rang, and nobody came, and then the wrong ones came. We drowned it after, for shame. And now it rings by itself.
fail_say: It was a long time ago. I was small. I remember the sound, that's all. Only the sound.

label: Some things are better left under the water.
say: ...Maybe you're right. Maybe it is ringing for me, and I should just go to it.
Leave it, then. I'll stop my ears. I've had practice.

line: The bell of {ruin_was} hangs in {town} now, and once a year it is rung for the dead of {ruin}, and only once. {keeper} counts the strokes.
Raised, and hung, and rung once for every soul of {ruin_was}. Under {water}, nothing rings back.
The bell rings over {town} again. On still nights, something in the crypt under {ruin} rings back.
{keeper} wept to hear it. The fishers say the water by {ruin} has gone cold, and stays cold.
The bell stays under {water}. {keeper} sits by the water at night and listens, and does not say what for.
Left where it lies. The bell of {ruin_was} still rings on still nights, and {keeper} has stopped asking anyone.
{keeper} was found by {water} at dawn, sitting up, eyes open, facing {ruin}. The bell had rung all night.
{keeper} went down to the water on a still night and did not come back. The bell has not rung since.

title: The drowned bell
The bell under {water}
What rings under {water}
stakes: the bell of {ruin_was}, and the peace of {keeper}
{keeper}'s last wish, and the drowned bell
plea: You heard it. Don't tell me you didn't. That's the bell of {ruin_was}, {ruin_years} under the water, and it rings for us who are left. I am the last. Bring it up. Bring it out of the crypt at {ruin} and let it be hung where it can be seen, before it rings for me.

Every still night since the spring. The bell of {ruin}. I was born under it. They threw it in the water the year {ruin_fall}, and I thought it was done with us. Raise it. Please. I want to hear it once in the light.
first: On still nights a bell rings under {water}: the bell of {ruin_was}, drowned {ruin_years} ago. {keeper} wants it raised from the crypt under {ruin}.
{keeper}, the last of {ruin_was}, wants its drowned bell brought up from {ruin}.
news_lapse: In {town}, the old {keeper_title} {keeper} was found dead by {water}, facing the ruins of {ruin}.
